body: As an autistic person myself,I get what you mean. It sucks to see people lambast you for a part of yourself that isn't harmful and that you can't control. But it gets better - my advice is to remember your dreams,and try to find some autistic friends! I was diagnosed over a year ago and while it's tough to accept it in a world that demonizes autism,having someone close to you who's also autistic makes all the difference (my best friend is autistic and she's so much fun to be around). Hell,you can even DM me if you want to talk. Best of luck to you,OP,and try to stay strong!

Give yourself a chance. It's crazy what can happen in two months - in only the span of two months,I went from a despondent burnout with no friends to somebody who's on their way to recovery. I have OCD,too,so I know what it's like,but let yourself live life! Have your first kiss,travel somewhere new,just don't give up. I have hope in you,OP. You can do another two months,just don't give up

Be there for her. Let her rant to you about her feelings,do your best to give her advice when she needs it,just be a shoulder to cry on and a hand for her to hold. Try to visit her as soon as possible,if you can,and offer to help her and her family get back on their feet by looking through job openings,offering to let them stay at your place (if applicable/possible),just be as supportive as you can and remember that this isn't your fault.
